newsitem.title: UK: Hanson completes demerger as Energy Group goes solo.
newsitem.headline: Hanson completes demerger as Energy Group goes solo.

text.p: Once mighty Hanson Plc turned on Monday into a humble building materials group as the former conglomerate completed its four-way demerger process with the spin-off of the Energy Group.

The Group, which consists of U.S.-Australian Peabody Coal and Britain's regional electricity company Eastern, saw its shares rise at their debut after the company reported a 38 percent rise in operating profit.
The operating profit was 138 million pounds ($224 million) in the three months to December 31 when Energy Group was still part of Hanson.
The debut of Energy Group on the London Stock Exchange coincided with the agreed bid by American Electric Power Co Inc for Yorkshire Electricity Group .

The offer triggered renewed takeover speculation in the electrity sector and helped push Energy Group's shares to 552-1/2 pence, 27-1/2 pence higher than they were trading on the grey market prior to the demerger.
The share price gives the new company a market value of nearly 2.9 billion pounds compared with less than 1.9 billion pounds for the Hanson rump.
Sahres in former blue chip Hanson eased two pence to 285-1/2 and may drop out of the FTSE 100 index after the next review on March 12.
Hanson, which used to epitomise the empire-building of the booming 1980s, earlier hived off Imperial Tobacco and Millennium Chemicals in a bid to streamline its widely diversified operations.

"With all the demergers completed successfully, we can now give full attention to 'building for the future'," said business tycoon Lord Hanson, who formed the former conglomerate and who remains chairman of the building materials rump.
The upturn in the British housing market has helped brick sales and Hanson expects demand for other building products to pick up too, although market conditions remains difficult.
Hanson said pre-tax profit, including Energy Group, fell to 157 million pounds in the last three months of 1996 from 248 million a year ago.
But the comparative figure included 205 million pounds of profits from businesses which have been demerged or sold later in the year, Hanson added.
The Energy Group, meanwhile, said its profits were boosted by its British electricity business. Results of the mining arm remained flat.
"It is a great start for the Energy Group. We are enthusiastic about the prospects for the future," said executive chairman Derek Bonham.
He earlier ruled out a further demerger to split the mining business from the electricity operations, which some analysts had said did not make a logical mix.
"The Energy Group has an enviable position across the power industry and we are confident that 1997 will prove a period of real progress," Bonham said on Monday. ($1=.6168 Pound)
